articles.title: HCLTech Just Landed a $1.14 Billion AI Deal With a European Giant. It's the Biggest New Contract in Years.
articles.excerpt: The Noida-headquartered IT services firm will build an AI-driven operating model for a major unnamed European company — entirely new business, not a renewal.
articles.image_caption: HCLTech CEO C Vijayakumar, who has steered the company's pivot toward AI-led transformation services
articles.nri_angle: HCLTech employs tens of thousands of Indian-origin engineers in the US and Europe — a mega deal of this size signals continued demand for Indian tech talent globally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Sending Its Top Trade Bodies to Washington Next Week. They're Going to Fight a $30 Billion Tariff.
articles.excerpt: FICCI, CII, the Commerce Ministry and three industry associations will testify before the USTR on July 8, arguing that America's forced-labour findings are legally flawed and economically destructive.
articles.image_caption: The Winder Building in Washington, D.C., headquarters of the Office of the United States Trade Representative
articles.nri_angle: If the 12.5% tariff takes effect, it could raise prices on Indian goods in the US, disrupt supply chains that employ diaspora professionals, and complicate the bilateral trade deal that affects everything from H-1B policies to student visa reciprocity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Handed India's Government Its Biggest Cheque Ever. Here's Why It Matters.
articles.excerpt: A record ₹2.87 lakh crore dividend — earned largely from defending the rupee during the Iran war — has compressed India's fiscal deficit to just 9.6% of the full-year target in two months. But the real test lies ahead.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: India's fiscal health directly affects rupee stability, bond yields and the investment climate that NRIs navigate for remittances, property and portfolio decisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Is Spending $500 Billion on Defence. It Wants India to Help Build the Arsenal.
articles.excerpt: From expelled diplomats to a full defence dialogue in four months — Canada and India are engineering one of the fastest diplomatic turnarounds in recent memory, with a free trade deal and a Modi visit to Ottawa on the horizon.
articles.image_caption: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who has spearheaded a dramatic reset in India-Canada relations since taking office
articles.nri_angle: The India-Canada reset directly affects nearly two million Indian-Canadians through improved visa processing, trade corridors, security cooperation and the political normalisation of a relationship that had turned hostile under Trudeau.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Private Rocket Is Ten Days From Orbit. The Startup Behind It Just Became a Unicorn.
articles.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace has set a July 12 launch window for Vikram-1, aiming to become only the fourth private company in the world to place a satellite in orbit from its own launch vehicle.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh at Sriharikota in November 2022
articles.nri_angle: Indian space startups are opening a new pathway for diaspora investors and technologists to participate in India's $44 billion commercial space economy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Just Banned New Petrol Two-Wheelers From 2028. The Capital's ₹15,000 Crore EV Gamble Is Now Live.
articles.excerpt: India's most polluted major city has launched its most aggressive electric vehicle policy yet, offering full tax waivers, scrappage cash, and a hard deadline to phase out internal combustion engines for key vehicle categories.
articles.image_caption: Inauguration of electric vehicle charging points at NITI Aayog premises in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: Delhi's EV push creates a direct investment corridor for NRI capital into India's electric mobility infrastructure, from charging networks to EV manufacturing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shah Rukh Khan Opens America’s First Franchise-Built Cricket Stadium in Los Angeles
articles.excerpt: The $21 million Knight Riders Cricket Ground hosted its inaugural MLC match and will serve as a venue for cricket’s return to the Olympics in 2028
articles.image_caption: Shah Rukh Khan, co-owner of the Knight Riders Group, inaugurated the Knight Riders Cricket Ground in Los Angeles on July 1, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: For 4.8 million Indian Americans who grew up watching cricket, the first franchise-owned cricket stadium in LA built by Bollywood icon SRK marks a milestone ahead of cricket’s 2028 Olympic return.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: While America Fights Its Data Centers, India Is Rolling Out the Red Carpet. The Numbers Are Staggering.
articles.excerpt: Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon are pouring tens of billions into Indian data centers. Zero taxes until 2047, no public hearings, and tenfold capacity growth projected over the next decade.
articles.image_caption: Inside a modern data center server room with rows of computing infrastructure
articles.nri_angle: Indian-Americans in tech work at the very companies now investing billions in India's data-center infrastructure — the buildout creates jobs, deepens the US-India tech partnership, and opens new investment opportunities from Lightstorm's IPO to semiconductor JVs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Is About to End a 30-Year Student Visa Rule. No Country Has More at Stake Than India.
articles.excerpt: A proposed rule eliminating 'Duration of Status' would cap F-1 stays at four years, slash grace periods, and threaten the Day-1 CPT pathway that thousands of Indian graduates depend on.
articles.image_caption: International students at an American university campus
articles.nri_angle: Indian students are 48% of all OPT participants in the US; the rule change could upend the F-1-to-H-1B pipeline that hundreds of thousands of Indian graduates depend on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Factories Are Cooling Off. The Warning Signs Are Hard to Ignore.
articles.excerpt: Manufacturing growth slipped to its second-weakest pace in four years in June, with export orders at a 39-month low and hiring at its softest this year — even as KPIT Technologies crashed 17% on a European demand shock.
articles.image_caption: Workers on a production line at an Indian manufacturing facility
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors should note that India's manufacturing momentum is fading even as equity valuations remain elevated; European demand weakness impacts IT and engineering outsourcing sectors that employ many diaspora professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asia's AI Bubble Just Popped. India Barely Flinched.
articles.excerpt: South Korea's KOSPI crashed 8% and foreign investors dumped $137 billion from Asian stocks in six months. India rose. Here's why the rotation may be just beginning.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, home of the Sensex index
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with US-based 401(k) and brokerage exposure to South Korean and Taiwanese tech ETFs face a direct portfolio rotation question as India emerges as the safer alternative.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Called Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee an Illegal Tax. The White House Is Fighting Back.
articles.excerpt: The ruling could reshape the economics of hiring foreign workers in America. Indian physicians, engineers, and their employers are caught in the legal crossfire.
articles.image_caption: A United States federal courthouse, where the H-1B fee ruling was decided
articles.nri_angle: The $100,000 fee directly affects the roughly 400,000 Indian-origin H-1B holders in the US, their employers, and anyone considering a job change or new petition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Japan Just Agreed to Build a Warship Antenna Together. It's Their First Joint Defence Project Ever.
articles.excerpt: The UNICORN naval mast, 10 new cooperation pacts, and a yen-rupee settlement plan: the 16th India-Japan summit delivered more than ceremony.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who signed the UNICORN defense pact with Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi
articles.nri_angle: The yen-rupee settlement framework could reduce remittance costs, and the AI pact opens pathways for Indian tech professionals seeking opportunities in Japan's labour-starved economy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Told WhatsApp to Freeze Its Biggest Privacy Update. Half a Billion Users Are in Limbo.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi has given Meta three days to explain how its username feature won't become a playground for scammers — or face regulatory action
articles.image_caption: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, whose ministry ordered WhatsApp to freeze its privacy policy update (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs depend on WhatsApp more than almost any other app to stay connected with family in India — any feature change or government restriction directly affects how the diaspora communicates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Startup Funding Fell 9% in the First Half of 2026. But Five New Unicorns Say That's Not the Whole Story.
articles.excerpt: AI investment exploded 317%, Bengaluru captured more than half of all capital, and 75% of listed startups are now profitable — the ecosystem is maturing, not shrinking
articles.image_caption: The Bengaluru skyline — India's startup capital saw five new unicorns in H1 2026 even as total funding fell 9 per cent (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's startup ecosystem is increasingly shaped by diaspora founders, investors, and returnees — the shift from volume to quality funding directly affects NRI angels and LP allocations to India-focused VC funds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Ram Mandir Donation Scandal Has Reached ₹200 Crore. Eight Are in Jail. Fifty More Are Under the Scanner.
articles.excerpt: CCTV caught temple staff skimming cash from donation boxes. Investigators found a 70-room hostel, luxury cars, and a paper trail that may stretch far beyond the eight arrests.
articles.image_caption: The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya during its inauguration ceremony in January 2024
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs donated to the Ram Mandir construction fund, and the embezzlement scandal directly undermines the trust diaspora communities placed in the temple administration.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Sending a Governor and a Deputy Minister to Khamenei’s Funeral. The Guest List Says Everything.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi’s delegation is carefully calibrated — senior enough to honour Tehran, restrained enough not to antagonise Washington. The oil price, the rupee, and Chabahar are all on the line.
articles.image_caption: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader for 36 years, killed in US-Israeli strikes in February 2026
articles.nri_angle: The US-Iran relationship directly shapes oil prices, the rupee’s value, and the cost of living for Indian families in India and abroad — the funeral period is a volatile window.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Green Card Categories Just Shut Down for Indians in a Single Month
articles.excerpt: The July 2026 Visa Bulletin has made EB-2 and EB-5 completely unavailable for India while pushing EB-1 further backwards — leaving hundreds of thousands of professionals in limbo until at least October.
articles.image_caption: A United States permanent resident card, commonly known as a green card
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals on H-1B visas face an indefinite freeze on their green card applications, with EB-2 completely shut and EB-1 moving backwards.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US and India Are in 'Sensitive' Talks Over Who Gets Access to the World's Most Powerful AI
articles.excerpt: Washington says it's taking a 'gradual, measured approach' to releasing Anthropic's frontier models to India. New Delhi says it needs guarantees that access won't be yanked away.
articles.image_caption: Jacob Helberg, U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Growth, Energy, and the Environment
articles.nri_angle: For the 300,000 Indians in the U.S. tech ecosystem and India's growing AI sector, reliable access to frontier AI models will determine whether Indian companies can compete on the global stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Stock Market Just Clawed Back to $5 Trillion. Here's What Turned the Tide.
articles.excerpt: A 42% crash in oil prices, a steadier rupee, and a wave of RBI measures have brought global funds back to Indian equities after months of record outflows.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's financial capital
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who weathered the May rout are seeing significant recovery gains as India-focused ETFs in the US turn positive for the first time in over a month.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Cheap Chinese AI Model Is Catching America's Best. India's Tech Sector Is in the Crossfire.
articles.excerpt: Beijing-based Zhipu AI's GLM-5.2 nearly matches OpenAI and Anthropic at a fraction of the cost — and US restrictions on its own models are making the problem worse.
articles.image_caption: An NVIDIA H100 GPU, the kind of AI chip powering both American and Chinese frontier models
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI leaders at US tech giants face an awkward paradox: their own government's export restrictions are empowering a Chinese competitor, while Indian developers gain access to cheaper frontier-grade models.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Now Selling Gasoline to Russia. The World's Energy Map Just Flipped.
articles.excerpt: Ukrainian drone strikes have knocked out 30% of Russia's refining capacity. India — Moscow's biggest crude buyer — is shipping finished fuel back.
articles.image_caption: Oil tankers docked at a fuel terminal for loading refined petroleum products
articles.nri_angle: India's growing leverage as the world's refining hub reshapes the energy dynamic NRIs have watched since 2022 — and may eventually influence global fuel prices for diaspora communities worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Named Its Two Biggest Fears. One of Them Is AI.
articles.excerpt: India's central bank warns that a global AI stock bubble and AI-powered cyberattacks are the most serious threats to the financial system — even as it declares banks healthier than ever.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters tower in Mumbai

sources.label: Reserve Bank of India Financial Stability Report

articles.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to both Indian and US equities need to weigh the RBI's warning that an AI-led sell-off in American markets could cascade into Indian stocks through wealth effects and capital outflows.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microsoft Is Building a 3,600-Km Undersea Cable From India to Singapore. The AI Data Race Just Went Submarine.
articles.excerpt: A consortium led by Lightstorm, backed by Microsoft, Tata Communications, Singtel, and NEC, will lay the I-2SEA cable to feed India's exploding demand for AI and cloud bandwidth — landing it in the same Andhra Pradesh town where Meta and Google are building data centers.
articles.image_caption: Submarine cable infrastructure supporting global internet connectivity
articles.nri_angle: Lower-latency submarine cables between India and SE Asia directly improve cloud and AI services for NRI tech workers and companies operating across both regions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Opened the Door to Chinese Investment. Its Electronics Giants Walked the Other Way.
articles.excerpt: Four months after New Delhi eased Press Note 3 to fast-track Chinese capital, India's biggest contract manufacturers have signed at least eight new partnerships — almost all with Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea.
articles.image_caption: Printed circuit board assembly in an electronics manufacturing facility
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors and tech professionals tracking India's electronics manufacturing boom need to understand the supply chain's deliberate tilt toward democratic partners over Chinese alternatives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Saved Birthright Citizenship. No Community Had More at Stake Than Indian Americans.
articles.excerpt: With green card backlogs stretching past a century, tens of thousands of Indian families in the U.S. faced losing their children's citizenship. The 6-3 ruling shuts that door.
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Indian families on H-1B and green card backlogs are among those most protected by the ruling, as their U.S.-born children's citizenship was directly threatened by Trump's executive order.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Bonds Just Had Their Best Month in Seven Years. The World's Biggest Index May Be Next.
articles.excerpt: After scrapping all taxes on foreign bond investment, India attracted a record $3.16 billion in June. Now Bloomberg index inclusion is on the horizon — and the real flood hasn't started yet.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: The tax reforms also incentivize NRI deposits and make Indian government bonds — yielding 6.74% with no capital gains or withholding tax — significantly more attractive for diaspora investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Just Had Its Worst Quarter Since COVID. India May Be the Biggest Winner.
articles.excerpt: Brent crude crashed 43% from its April war peak to below $71 — erasing the entire Iran conflict premium and handing India a potential $30 billion annual import savings.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker off the coast of Yemen, near the shipping lanes that connect to the Strait of Hormuz
articles.nri_angle: Cheaper crude means lower petrol and cooking gas prices in India, a weaker current account deficit that stabilises the rupee, and reduced inflation pressure — all of which directly affect NRI remittances, investments, and family costs back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The EU Is About to Restrict the Raw Materials India Needs Most. New Delhi Is Scrambling for Exemptions.
articles.excerpt: Europe's planned ban on metal scrap exports to non-OECD countries and its 47% cut to tariff-free steel imports could raise costs for Indian manufacturers — just as a landmark trade deal between the two is set to take effect.
articles.image_caption: The European Commission's Berlaymont headquarters in Brussels — the body behind the Critical Raw Materials Act that could restrict India's access to key industrial inputs
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with business interests in Indian manufacturing or real estate should watch closely — rising steel and aluminium costs could push up construction prices, infrastructure project timelines, and the cost of everything from vehicles to appliances.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Killed a 90-Year Rule That Kept Agency Chiefs Safe From the President
articles.excerpt: The 6-3 ruling overturns Humphrey's Executor, giving Trump — and every future president — the power to fire the heads of more than two dozen independent agencies at will. For Indian Americans in government and the industries these agencies oversee, the stakes are enormous.
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C., at dusk
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans hold leadership positions across federal agencies and dominate the tech and finance sectors these regulators oversee — a shift in agency independence directly affects their careers, investments, and consumer protections.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Cut Jet Fuel Prices for the First Time Since the Iran War. IndiGo Is Already Passing It On.
articles.excerpt: Aviation turbine fuel drops ₹5 per litre to ₹110 in Delhi — the first reduction since the Middle East conflict sent prices to record highs. On the same day, India's largest airline launches a stripped-down fare class that could reshape how the diaspora books flights home.
articles.image_caption: An IndiGo Airbus A320neo aircraft in the airline's signature livery
articles.nri_angle: Jet fuel accounts for up to 40% of airline operating costs — this price cut and IndiGo's new budget fare could make trips to India measurably cheaper for millions of NRIs who fly home at least once a year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Shipped Its First Semiconductor Chips Abroad. The Third Factory Starts This Month.
articles.excerpt: CG Semi's Sanand plant sent its first commercial chip shipment to Malaysia in June — and India's semiconductor mission is about to cross another threshold as a third plant goes live in July.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor clean room — the controlled environment where chips are assembled and tested
articles.nri_angle: NRI semiconductor professionals in the Bay Area and globally now have a growing domestic chip ecosystem to engage with through design incentives and manufacturing opportunities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New Army Chief Has a Five-Letter Plan to Reshape the World's Largest Volunteer Force
articles.excerpt: General Dhiraj Seth, the first officer from the Armoured Corps to lead the Army in nearly three decades, has unveiled a 'VIJAY' framework centred on AI, drones and soldier welfare.
articles.image_caption: General Dhiraj Seth after receiving a guard of honour as the 31st Chief of Army Staff at South Block, New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: India's new Army chief will deepen the US-India defence partnership and expand opportunities for diaspora entrepreneurs in India's growing private defence sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian-Origin CEO Just Raised $800 Million to Challenge Big Tech's AI Monopoly
articles.excerpt: Noida-born Vipul Ved Prakash's Together AI has more than doubled its valuation to $8.3 billion, with annual bookings crossing $1.15 billion — all on the back of open-source models.
articles.image_caption: Vipul Ved Prakash, founder and CEO of Together AI
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEO Vipul Ved Prakash, who grew up coding in Noida, now leads one of the world's most valuable AI startups — validating the diaspora's outsized role in shaping global AI infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Had Its Driest June in Over a Decade. July May Not Be Much Better.
articles.excerpt: The fifth-driest June since 1901, a strengthening El Niño, and a 23% lag in crop planting are raising alarms over food security and economic growth in the world's most populous nation.
articles.image_caption: Monsoon clouds over India, where June 2026 rainfall fell 40% below the long-term average
articles.nri_angle: Poor monsoon years historically trigger higher remittance demands from rural families and affect NRI investment sentiment in agriculture-linked sectors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Tata Breach That Exposed Apple's Most Guarded Secrets
articles.excerpt: A ransomware group has dumped 200,000 files from Tata Electronics onto the dark web — including iPhone 18 Pro supplier maps, component lists, and prototype photos. India's Make in India manufacturing dream just got its biggest cybersecurity test.
articles.image_caption: Bombay House, the Tata Group headquarters in Mumbai — subsidiary Tata Electronics suffered a data breach that exposed Apple supply chain secrets (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's credibility as a secure global manufacturing hub directly affects diaspora professionals in the tech supply chain and NRI investment confidence in India's industrial growth story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US-India Trade Deal Is '99% Done.' Here's What's Left — and What's at Stake.
articles.excerpt: US Ambassador Sergio Gor says only the last one per cent remains, but behind the optimism lies a fraught final stretch over agriculture, tariffs, and the political will to close.
articles.image_caption: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor at the USISPF Leadership Summit in Washington
articles.nri_angle: A stable US-India trade deal would ease uncertainty for NRI professionals and entrepreneurs navigating tariffs, visa linkages, and bilateral business corridors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Opened the World's First Nuclear-Powered Hydrogen Plant. No Other Country Has Done This.
articles.excerpt: The Kalpakkam facility uses heat from a fast breeder reactor to split water without burning a single gram of fossil fuel — a technology the rest of the world is still chasing.
articles.image_caption: The nuclear facility at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, home to India's Fast Breeder Test Reactor and the world's first nuclear hydrogen plant
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in clean energy, nuclear engineering, and hydrogen sectors could see new corridors for technology transfer and professional opportunities as India commercialises this first-of-its-kind technology.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Quad Foreign Ministers Will Meet in the Philippines This Month. A Trump Visit to India May Follow.
articles.excerpt: US Ambassador Sergio Gor confirmed the Manila meeting on the sidelines of ASEAN and revealed plans for a Quad leaders' summit — potentially bringing President Trump back to India.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Modi with Quad leaders at the 2024 summit; the grouping's foreign ministers will meet again in Manila this month
articles.nri_angle: The Quad's deepening architecture directly shapes the security and trade environment for NRIs with business or professional ties across both countries, and a Trump visit to India would signal durable partnership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Japan's PM Just Landed in India With 150 Business Leaders and a $61 Billion Promise
articles.excerpt: Sanae Takaichi's first official visit to India kicks off the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit in New Delhi, with trade, defence, high-speed rail, and the Indo-Pacific on the agenda.
articles.image_caption: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who arrived in New Delhi on July 1 for the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit
articles.nri_angle: Over 46,000 Indians live in Japan; the deepening partnership means easier work visas, more Japanese investment in Indian companies, and growing opportunities for Indian tech professionals at Japanese multinationals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's UPI Just Went Live in Greece. That's 10 Countries and Counting.
articles.excerpt: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal witnessed the Eurobank-NPCI partnership launch in Athens, as India's digital payment system continues its quiet conquest of global finance.
articles.image_caption: A customer scans a QR code to make a mobile payment — the technology powering India's UPI global expansion
articles.nri_angle: India's 18.7 million NRIs stand to save billions as UPI remittance corridors expand to 10 countries and counting, offering faster and cheaper alternatives to traditional bank transfers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kotak Mahindra Just Bought Deutsche Bank's Entire India Retail Business for $30 Million
articles.excerpt: The deal hands Kotak 150,000 customers, ₹29,000 crore in loans, and a wealth management book that Deutsche Bank spent decades building — all for the price of a Manhattan apartment block.
articles.image_caption: Deutsche Bank headquarters in Frankfurt — the German lender is exiting India retail banking
articles.nri_angle: NRIs banking through Deutsche Bank in India will transition to Kotak Mahindra, reflecting the growing dominance of Indian private banks over foreign lenders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India’s Carmakers Just Posted Their Best June Ever. Maruti Crossed 200,000 in a Single Month.
articles.excerpt: Maruti Suzuki set an all-time monthly record, Mahindra’s sales surged 37%, and exports are booming — even as Europe’s automakers issue profit warnings and cut jobs.
articles.image_caption: A Maruti Suzuki vehicle on an Indian road — the carmaker just crossed 200,000 units sold in a single month
articles.nri_angle: Indian auto stocks are among the best performers this year as domestic sales and exports hit records, offering a compelling investment thesis for NRI portfolios at a time when Western automakers are retrenching.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Replaced Its Biggest Rural Jobs Programme. Not Everyone Thinks the Replacement Is an Upgrade.
articles.excerpt: MGNREGA is dead. The new VB-G RAM G scheme promises 125 days of work — but states, including BJP ones, say the funding model could bankrupt them.
articles.image_caption: MGNREGA workers removing mud from a dry pond under the rural employment programme
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRI families send remittances to relatives in rural India who depend on MGNREGA wages as a safety net — any disruption or state-level funding shortfall directly affects those households.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Trade Deal With a Western Economy in Decades Goes Live in Two Weeks. Here's What Changes.
articles.excerpt: The India-UK CETA comes into force on July 15 with tariff cuts, professional mobility provisions and the end of double social security payments for Indian workers in Britain.
articles.image_caption: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who led a 170-member delegation to London for CETA implementation talks
articles.nri_angle: The 1.9 million Indian-origin residents in the UK stand to benefit from eliminated double social security payments, smoother professional mobility and lower tariffs on goods traded between the two countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Hired Uber's India Boss to Run Its Second-Largest Market
articles.excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh, who spent a decade building Uber across India and South Asia, will take over as OpenAI's first managing director for India in September — a market with 100 million weekly ChatGPT users.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman — the company has appointed former Uber India head Prabhjeet Singh as its first India managing director (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech leaders are increasingly moving into AI-native companies, signalling that India is becoming a primary AI market, not just a talent source.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Factory Engine Just Hit Its Second-Lowest Gear in Four Years
articles.excerpt: June manufacturing PMI slipped to 54.2 as cooling demand and Europe's shrinking appetite for Indian goods dragged on output, hiring and business confidence.
articles.image_caption: ILO in Asia and the Pacific via flickr (BY-ND)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with Indian equity exposure should watch for PMI-driven valuation corrections in capital goods and industrial stocks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Eight Arrested in Ayodhya Ram Temple Donation Scam. Now the Supreme Court Is Being Asked to Step In.
articles.excerpt: A PIL demands a CBI probe and forensic audit of the Ram Janmabhoomi Trust, the local bar association has refused to defend the accused, and NRI donors who sent crores are demanding answers.
articles.image_caption: The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, consecrated by Prime Minister Modi in January 2024
articles.nri_angle: NRI communities in the US, UK, Canada and Middle East donated crores to the Ram Mandir construction — the embezzlement scandal and demand for a forensic audit of digital payment records directly affects diaspora donors who contributed through online portals and UPI.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran and Oman Want to Charge Ships $40 Billion a Year to Pass Through the Strait of Hormuz. India Just Became the Biggest Loser.
articles.excerpt: A formal toll proposal for the world's most important oil chokepoint would hit India's crude import bill harder than any other major economy — and the 60-day grace period expires in mid-August.
articles.image_caption: Cargo ships and oil tankers near storage terminals — the Strait of Hormuz carries a fifth of the world's oil supply
articles.nri_angle: A permanent Hormuz toll would pressure the rupee and reignite inflation in India, directly affecting NRI remittance values, Indian equity returns, and the cost of living for families back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'PoK Is Not Part of Pakistan': Thousands Protest in Rawalakot as Azad Kashmir Unrest Enters Fourth Week
articles.excerpt: At least 53 civilians killed as Pakistan deploys army, bans protest movement, and shuts down internet across the disputed territory — while diaspora communities rally in the UK
articles.image_caption: View of Muzaffarabad, the capital of Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir, where protests have brought the city to a standstill
articles.nri_angle: 1.5 million Kashmiris in the UK and tens of thousands across North America retain deep ties to protest-hit cities like Mirpur and Rawalakot; diaspora communities have staged counter-protests in Bradford and other cities
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
